overview: TotalEnergies is a French integrated energy major, one of the world's largest oil and gas companies, operating across the full hydrocarbon value chain (exploration & production, LNG, refining, petrochemicals, and fuels/lubricants marketing) while building a growing Integrated Power business in renewables, batteries and gas-fired generation. The Company produced about 2.53 Mboe/d of hydrocarbons and 48 TWh of net electricity in 2025, is the world's 3rd-largest LNG player (43.9 Mt sold), and is active in roughly 120 countries with around 101,500 employees. TotalEnergies reports in US dollars (it switched its primary reporting currency from EUR to USD starting FY2012, reflecting that oil, gas and LNG are priced globally in dollars); this project's database normalizes TTE.PA financials to USD throughout, consistent with the Company's own reporting basis since FY2012 and with peers Shell, BP, Chevron and ExxonMobil.

business_model.summary: TotalEnergies monetizes hydrocarbon reserves and growing low-carbon power generation through five reporting segments. Exploration & Production (E&P) and Integrated LNG together form the 'hydrocarbons' growth pillar, generating the bulk of cash flow from oil/gas sales and are highly leveraged to Brent, Henry Hub, TTF and JKM prices. Refining & Chemicals and Marketing & Services (the Downstream) convert crude into fuels, petrochemicals and lubricants sold through ~13,000 service stations and B2B channels, earning margin-based (not price-based) income. Integrated Power is the second strategic growth pillar: renewables (solar/wind), battery storage, gas-fired flexible capacity, and B2B/B2C power and gas retail (6.0 million power clients, 2.7 million gas clients). Revenue is largely transactional/commodity-linked (spot and contract sales of oil, gas, LNG, power and refined products) rather than subscription-based, though long-term LNG offtake contracts and power purchase agreements provide multi-year revenue visibility. Customers span national oil companies and utilities (B2B upstream/LNG offtake), industrial/wholesale buyers (petrochemicals, bulk fuels), and retail consumers (service stations, residential power/gas).

revenue_streams.name: Exploration & Production
revenue_streams.note: 2025 adjusted net operating income $8.40B (46% of segment total); production +4% YoY to 2,529 kboe/d on project ramp-ups (Mero 2-4 Brazil, Anchor/Ballymore US, Tyra Denmark)

revenue_streams.name: Integrated LNG
revenue_streams.note: 2025 adjusted net operating income $4.11B; 43.9 Mt LNG sold (3rd largest global LNG player), 15.1 Mt from equity production; North Field East (Qatar) and Costa Azul (Mexico) start-ups expected to drive 2026 growth

revenue_streams.name: Integrated Power
revenue_streams.note: 2025 adjusted net operating income $2.22B; net power production +17% YoY to 48.1 TWh (31.4 TWh renewables); installed renewable capacity 34.1 GW, +8 GW YoY; EPH flexible-power acquisition (Europe) completing mid-2026

revenue_streams.name: Refining & Chemicals
revenue_streams.note: 2025 adjusted net operating income $2.38B, down from $4.65B in 2023 on weaker petrochemical margins; European Refining Margin (ERM) more than doubled to ~$33/b by Q3 2026 amid Middle East-driven supply disruption

revenue_streams.name: Marketing & Services
revenue_streams.note: 2025 adjusted net operating income $1.37B; petroleum product sales volumes down 5% as portfolio is focused toward higher-margin activity; ~13,000 service stations in ~60 countries

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B (national oil companies, utilities, LNG offtakers, industrial/petrochemical buyers, power/gas wholesale) and B2C (retail fuel, power and gas customers; ~2 million individual shareholders)
business_model.geographic_mix: Hydrocarbon production 2025: Middle East & North Africa ~34%, Africa (excl. North Africa) ~17%, Americas ~18%, Europe ~21%, Asia-Pacific ~10%. Downstream sales concentrated in Europe (~55-58% of M&S volumes) with growing Americas/Asia-Pacific presence. Reporting currency USD since FY2012; listed primarily on Euronext Paris with an NYSE ADR (TTE).

competitive_position.market_position: One of the six oil 'supermajors' and the world's 3rd-largest LNG player (~10% of global LNG market, targeting ~60 Mt/y by 2030). Mid-sized relative to ExxonMobil and Chevron by market cap and net income (H1 2026 net profit of $11.2B vs. Exxon's ~$18.7B, Chevron's ~$14.3B, Shell's ~$16.5B), but differentiated by the fastest-growing Integrated Power platform among the majors and a track record of low-cost, resilient upstream production (technical costs $16.5/boe, production costs $5.0/boe in 2025).

moat_factors.description: Vertical integration from upstream E&P through LNG, refining, petrochemicals and retail/power distribution smooths commodity-price volatility and captures margin across the chain
Pre-dividend organic cash breakeven of $26.4/b and production costs under $5/boe provide resilience in low oil-price environments versus higher-cost peers

3rd-largest global LNG player with long-term offtake agreements (North Field East, Costa Azul, Mozambique, Alaska LNG preliminary 20-year deal) providing contracted volume growth and counterparty relationships difficult for smaller players to replicate

moat_factors.factor: Balance sheet strength and capital discipline
moat_factors.description: Gearing targeted below 10% by end-2026 (13.1% at June 30, 2026, down from 17.9% a year earlier), supporting continued buybacks and dividend growth even through commodity cycles

moat_factors.factor: First-mover position in Integrated Power among majors
moat_factors.description: 34+ GW installed renewable capacity and a growing B2B/B2C power and gas client base (~8.7 million combined) give TotalEnergies a more developed low-carbon electricity platform than Exxon/Chevron, though still small relative to utilities
Century-long operating history and deep host-government relationships (Qatar, UAE, Nigeria, Angola, Iraq) support access to resource-rich but politically sensitive jurisdictions

weaknesses: Still fundamentally a price-taker on ~60% of adjusted operating income (E&P + Integrated LNG) exposed directly to Brent/TTF/JKM swings
Heavy exposure to the Middle East (34% of 2025 hydrocarbon production) concentrated in geopolitically volatile jurisdictions (Qatar, UAE, Iraq, Libya, Yemen)
Integrated Power remains sub-scale and lower-returning (ROACE ~9.7% in 2025) versus legacy hydrocarbon segments (E&P ROACE ~13.0%, Refining & Chemicals ~37.7%)
Minority stakes in sanctioned Russian entities (Novatek 19.4%, Yamal LNG 20.02%, Arctic LNG 2 10%) create ongoing legal, reputational and potential further impairment risk
Lower absolute scale and free cash flow generation than ExxonMobil and Chevron limits capacity to outspend peers on mega-projects

growth_drivers: LNG portfolio expansion toward ~60 Mt/y by 2030 (~50% growth), anchored by North Field East/South (Qatar), Mozambique LNG restart (targeting first LNG 2029), Costa Azul (Mexico) and a preliminary 20-year, 2 Mt/y offtake agreement from Alaska LNG

Integrated Power build-out: electricity production guided up ~25% in 2026 to exceed 60 TWh, helped by the EPH flexible-power asset acquisition in Europe (completing mid-2026) accelerating a gas-to-power integration strategy

Upstream production growth of ~3% per year through 2030 from project start-ups/ramp-ups (Mero 2-4 Brazil, Anchor/Ballymore US, Lapa Brazil, Ratawi Iraq, Tilenga Uganda, Tyra Denmark, Suriname GranMorgu, Namibia Venus) while holding production costs below $5/boe
Multi-year cash-savings program targeting $12.5 billion of Capex+Opex reduction over 2026-2030
Downstream margin recovery: European refining margins at historically high levels in 2026 (ERM >$30/b by Q3) due to Russian capacity unavailability and Middle East supply disruption to Asian refiners

Shareholder return growth: dividend policy of >5% annual growth through 2030, buybacks scaled up with oil price (Q4 2026 buyback authorization of $2.5B, full-year 2026 guidance well above the original $3-6B range given elevated Brent)
Secular LNG/gas demand growth as a transition fuel displacing coal, and growing global electricity demand (TotalEnergies targets >10% market share in LNG)

business.description: Results highly sensitive to Brent, Henry Hub, TTF, JKM and refining margins; TotalEnergies estimates a $10/b Brent move shifts adjusted operating income by ~$2.3B and CFFO by ~$2.8B per year

business.risk: Reserve replacement and project execution risk
business.description: Growth depends on complex, capital-intensive major projects (LNG, deepwater, renewables) subject to cost overruns, delays, partner/government negotiations and permitting risk
$3.9B of 2025 acquisitions (Malaysia offshore blocks, VSB, renewables in Canada/Dominican Republic/Uganda) and the pending EPH power-asset deal carry integration and synergy-realization risk
Network of 100,000+ suppliers across 150+ countries exposed to geopolitical and pandemic-related disruption

financial.description: ~$15.9B average floating-rate debt in 2025; a 1% SOFR move affects net income/cash flow by only ~$0.1B, a modest sensitivity
USD reporting currency since FY2012 but costs partly in EUR; a $0.10/EUR move affects adjusted operating income by only ~$0.1B, concentrated in Refining & Chemicals

financial.risk: Access to capital for hydrocarbon projects
financial.description: Growing divestment/exclusion policies among investors and lenders targeting fossil-fuel financing could raise TotalEnergies' cost of capital for oil and gas projects
Company flags a typical $2-3B temporary Q1 working-capital swing tied to hydrocarbon price/inventory timing

regulatory.description: EU-ETS allowance prices ~€75/t CO2 at end-2025, expected to exceed €100/t in Phase 4; TotalEnergies' internal planning case uses a $100/t CO2 price (potentially $200/t in a stress case), estimated to cut discounted asset value by ~15% in the stress scenario
Tightening climate regulation, investor ESG screening and potential demand destruction for hydrocarbons over the long term could impair the value of oil & gas reserves and refining assets

Exposure to evolving, sometimes uncoordinated international sanctions regimes (notably linked to Russia) that could restrict financing, access to USD markets, or operations in sanctioned jurisdictions
Climate-related litigation, Vigilance Plan obligations, and intense NGO/media scrutiny of a major fossil-fuel producer could affect reputation, market access and cost of capital

macro.description: A Middle East crisis beginning February 28, 2026 cut Company production by an estimated 5-10% (up to ~210 kboe/d in Q2 2026) due to Strait of Hormuz disruption affecting Qatar, Iraq and UAE offshore output; SATORP refinery in Saudi Arabia was damaged and ran at reduced capacity through much of 2026

19.4% stake in Novatek (no longer equity-accounted, ~$14.8B of cumulative 2022 impairments/provisions) and 20.02% in Yamal LNG ($5.8B carrying value at Dec 2025) remain exposed to further sanctions escalation or Russian government action

Mozambique LNG (26.5% TotalEnergies stake, ~$15-20B project) was under force majeure 2021-2025 due to Cabo Delgado insurgency; fully restarted January 2026 but security conditions in northern Mozambique remain a monitored risk ahead of targeted 2029 first LNG
A sustained economic slowdown would reduce oil, gas, refined-product and electricity demand, pressuring prices and margins across all segments

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global oil demand still growing modestly (~0.9 Mb/d in 2026 per IEA) led by non-OECD and petrochemical demand, while OPEC+ supply discipline and Middle East conflict-related disruption have pushed Brent and refining margins to multi-year highs in 2026 ($92/b average in H1 2026 vs. ~$72/b in H1 2025). LNG demand continues to grow structurally as a coal-displacement and energy-security fuel, particularly in Europe and Asia; global electricity demand growth (~2.8%/year) is accelerating on AI/data-center load and electrification, benefiting the Integrated Power pillar.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High for upstream/LNG/refining (directly linked to global commodity price cycles); moderate for Marketing & Services and Integrated Power (contracted/retail elements provide some stability)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (floating-rate debt ~$15.9B; 1% SOFR move ≈ $0.1B impact), though higher rates raise financing costs for capital-intensive LNG and renewables projects across the industry
key_input_costs: Steel, equipment and EPC costs for upstream/LNG/renewables megaprojects
Natural gas as feedstock/fuel for CCGT flexible power

recent_developments.event: Q3 2026 pre-announcement: European Refining Margin Marker (ERM) more than doubled quarter-on-quarter to ~$33/b from ~$13.5/b in Q2 2026; hydrocarbon production guided to 2.45-2.50 Mboe/d with Middle East conflict impact estimated at ~5% of total production; Integrated Power cash flow guided to $750-800 million

Board adopted a dividend policy targeting >5% annual dividend growth through 2030, reaffirmed shareholder returns of at least 40% of cash flow, set a gearing target below 10%, and authorized $2.5B of Q4 2026 buybacks (full-year 2026 buybacks tracking well above the original $3-6B guidance range given elevated oil prices)

H1 2026 adjusted net income of $11.4B (+47% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of $25.7B (+27% YoY) driven by Brent averaging $92.3/b (+28% YoY) amid the Middle East conflict; gearing fell to 13.1% at June 30, 2026 from 17.9% a year earlier

Middle East conflict beginning February 28, 2026 disrupted Strait of Hormuz transit, cutting Company production (Qatar, Iraq, UAE offshore) by an estimated 5-10%, damaged the SATORP refinery (Saudi Arabia, restarted at reduced capacity, targeting full capacity by end-Q3 2026), and pushed European gas prices to $16-20/MBtu and global refining margins to historic highs
Mozambique LNG fully restarted onshore and offshore activities at the Afungi site after the November 2025 lifting of the 2021 force majeure; targeting first LNG by 2029 from the 13 Mt/y plant

Integrated LNG growth continuing with North Field East (Qatar, 2 Mtpa offtake) and Costa Azul (Mexico Pacific coast) LNG start-ups in 2026, plus a preliminary 20-year, 2 Mt/y offtake agreement signed with the Alaska LNG project

Integrated Power M&A: completed acquisition of 50% of EPH's European flexible power generation portfolio (UK, Italy, Netherlands, France); relinquished certain US offshore wind concessions (awarded 2022) in exchange for lease-fee retrocession (~$555M TotalEnergies share), reflecting a pullback from US offshore wind amid a less favorable policy environment

FY2025 results: adjusted net income $15.6B (down from $18.3B in 2024) on lower Brent ($69/b average, down from $81/b) and weaker LNG prices, partly offset by record production (+4% YoY) and resilient Integrated Power performance; FY2025 payout ratio reached 55% of CFFO

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Patrick Pouyanné has emphasized a 'balanced and profitable transition strategy, anchored on two growth pillars: hydrocarbons and electricity,' while reiterating that the Company will wait for real stabilization in the Strait of Hormuz before restarting curtailed Middle East production, given the two-to-three-month lead time to resume output. Management has highlighted that higher oil and gas prices during the 2026 Middle East conflict have more than offset the lost production volumes, enabling the Company to raise shareholder returns (buybacks and a new multi-year >5% dividend growth policy) while simultaneously lowering gearing toward a sub-10% medium-term target.

bull_case: Elevated 2026 oil, gas and refining-margin environment (Brent ~$90-100/b, ERM >$30/b) driven by Middle East conflict and Russian capacity disruption is flowing straight through to record cash flow, funding both higher dividends (>5%/year growth policy through 2030) and larger buybacks

Low-cost, disciplined upstream portfolio (sub-$5/boe production costs, $26.4/b organic cash breakeven) and a multi-year $12.5B cost-savings program provide downside protection if oil prices normalize lower

LNG growth pipeline (North Field East/South, Costa Azul, Mozambique restart, Alaska offtake) underpins a path to ~60 Mt/y by 2030 and ~10% global LNG market share, a structurally growing, longer-duration cash flow stream

Integrated Power is scaling quickly (net power production +17% YoY in 2025, installed renewables +8 GW YoY) giving TotalEnergies the most developed low-carbon power platform among the oil majors, with optionality on the energy transition
Balance sheet has de-levered rapidly (gearing 13.1% at June 2026, down from 17.9% a year prior, targeting <10%), giving flexibility for further returns or opportunistic M&A

Valuation generally screens cheaply relative to US majors (forward multiples in the high single digits per some trackers), with consensus analyst ratings skewed toward Buy/Outperform and price targets implying upside from recent levels
bear_case: Current earnings are substantially inflated by a geopolitical shock (Middle East conflict since February 2026); if the conflict resolves and Brent/ERM normalize lower, adjusted net income and buyback capacity could fall sharply from 2026 levels

Heavy production concentration in the Middle East (34% of 2025 output) and history of force-majeure events (Yemen LNG since 2015, Mozambique LNG 2021-2025) show recurring vulnerability to regional conflict, terrorism and sanctions risk
Lingering Russia exposure (Novatek, Yamal LNG stakes) carries open-ended risk of further sanctions, impairments or forced divestment with limited company control over timing or value recovery

Energy transition and carbon-pricing risk is real and quantified by the Company itself: a $200/t CO2 stress scenario is estimated to cut discounted asset value by ~15%, while Integrated Power returns (ROACE ~9.7% in 2025) remain well below legacy hydrocarbon segments, questioning capital-allocation efficiency of the pivot

Downstream segments (Refining & Chemicals, Marketing & Services) remain structurally volatile and volume-declining in mature markets (Europe product sales down, petrochemical margins weak in 2023-2025 outside the current margin spike), limiting the durability of the current downstream earnings surge
